text.arabic_uthmani: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ رَبَّنَآ أَرِنَا ٱلَّذَيْنِ أَضَلَّانَا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِنَا لِيَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a new reported-speech scene as sequel to the prior verdict
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) does more than open another sentence. It carries the prior verdict into a fresh quoted scene, so the rejecters' words are heard as a sequel to punishment rather than as an isolated confession.

topics.headline: resumptive speech boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quoted plea is staged as sequel to the prior verdict, not as an isolated speech.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction is locally attached to the reporting clause and CRITICAL rows consistently read it as a boundary from verdict into exposed speech.

words.gloss_range: reported-speech verb that gathers a plural rejecting group into one quoted voice
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, reporting, and declaration; the local Form I perfect selects ordinary reported utterance as the frame of self-exposure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite plural relative subject completed by the following rejection clause

words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) places the whole request inside reported speech. Its preposed singular form gathers {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) into one collective voice, while the perfect makes their judgment-scene speech sound already staged for hearing. Because the quote moves straight into Lord-address, the ordinary speech verb becomes a speech-to-Lord frame under pressure. The blame-speech pattern also recalls condemned speakers blaming misleaders at 7:38, but here the target narrows into a dual pair.

topics.headline: singular verb gathers plural voice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one reported-speech frame gathers the plural rejecting group into a single collective voice.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a preposed singular perfect verb with the following plural relative subject and a quoted complement spanning the rest of the ayah.

topics.headline: speech as audible evidence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rejecters expose their own blame strategy through direct quotation rather than narrator paraphrase.
topics.reason: The ordinary Form I speech verb governs the full quote, so the judgment scene documents the group through its own utterance.

topics.headline: blame-speech distribution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this speech belongs to a wider judgment-blame pattern while still narrowing the blame into this ayah's dual target.
topics.reason: Distributional and concrete-reference rows, especially the blame speech at 7:38, support the local reported-speech frame without overriding its grammar.

words.gloss_range: definite plural relative subject, completed by the following rejection clause before the quote begins

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect plural rejection completing the relative identity of the speakers

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) delays the speakers' full identity until {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) completes the relative clause. The quote therefore arrives through a narrator-side label: this is not generic human distress, but the speech of a class already defined by rejection.

topics.headline: relative subject names the speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers are identified by a relative construction before their plea is heard.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun is the subject of the reporting verb and is completed by the following rejection clause, so identity precedes quotation.

words.gloss_range: perfect plural rejection with no stated object, making rejection the speakers' established identity before their plea
words.root_gloss_range: covering, denial, rejection, and ingratitude; the local objectless perfect selects established rejection while retaining covering-versus-disclosure pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Form IV imperative asking for caused disclosure to the speakers

words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) fixes culpability before the plea begins. Because the verb is perfect, plural, and objectless, rejection reads as an established identity-wide act. It also resumes the surah's rejection-and-judgment thread before the speakers try to recast their condition as caused misguidance; the covering/rejection field then sharpens the irony when the same speakers demand disclosure through {{ar:أَرِنَا}} ({{tr:arinā}}).

topics.headline: perfect objectless rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that rejection is already established as the speakers' identity before they address the Lord.
topics.reason: The perfect plural verb completes the relative clause with no explicit object, supporting an identity-wide rejection frame.

topics.headline: covering meets demand to see
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that those marked by covering and rejection now demand disclosure.
topics.reason: The local sense is active rejection, while the root's covering field survives as image pressure because the next request asks for showing.

topics.headline: surah rejection thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this identity label resumes the surah's rejection-and-judgment thread before the plea begins.
topics.reason: Distributional rows connect rejection with misguidance, lord-address, and speech under judgment, all of which are locally present.

words.gloss_range: direct vocative address, relationally claiming lordship through the first-person plural suffix
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, ownership, governance, sustaining authority, and nurture; the local construct vocative foregrounds claimed relation to governing authority
words.prose: {{ar:رَبَّنَآ}} ({{tr:rabbanā}}) is the first word inside the quote, an abrupt vocative with the address particle omitted. The suffix makes the rejecters claim relation to the Lord they had rejected, so lordship is invoked as governing authority for disclosure and retaliation. The blame-address scene recalls 7:38, while the contrast with the steadfast confession in 41:30 keeps this address morally exposed.

topics.headline: abrupt relational address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quote opens in direct address and that the speakers claim the Lord relation through the suffix.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the word as vocative before the request, and morphology makes the first-person plural relation explicit.

topics.headline: lordship invoked for disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plea appeals to governing lordship precisely when the speakers seek exposure and rank reversal.
topics.reason: The local title foregrounds governing authority and is syntactically tied to the imperative request that follows.

topics.headline: rejecters speak lord-address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony of rejecters using Lord-address in a blame scene, with 7:38 and 41:30 sharpening the contrast.
topics.reason: Concrete parallels include blamed speech at 7:38 and the contrasting steadfast confession at 41:30; both support the local irony without changing the vocative parse.

words.gloss_range: Form IV imperative of showing, with the speakers as recipients and the dual pair as the displayed object
words.root_gloss_range: seeing, showing, perceiving, and making known; the local Form IV imperative selects caused disclosure to the speakers

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative masculine dual relative pronoun as the displayed object

words.prose: {{ar:أَرِنَا}} ({{tr:arinā}}) is not simple seeing; it asks the Lord to make the speakers see. The first-person suffix makes them recipients of disclosure, and {{ar:ٱلَّذَيْنِ}} ({{tr:alladhayni}}) supplies the displayed dual object. That makes the reversal sharp: those marked by covering now demand visible evidence, a pattern that can be contrasted with reassurance requests such as 2:260 without changing the local blame setting.

topics.headline: imperative of caused disclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers ask to be made to see a specified dual object.
topics.reason: The Form IV imperative has the first-person plural suffix as recipient object and the following dual relative as the displayed object.

topics.headline: seeing confronts covering and hiddenness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that disclosure reverses both the speakers' covering identity and the hiddenness of the accused domain.
topics.reason: The seeing/showing root is locally licensed by the imperative, and adjacent source terms make hidden agency a live payoff.

topics.headline: show-us formula under judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the show-us request belongs to recognizable request patterns, while this instance is narrowed to blame after verdict.
topics.reason: Rows comparing requests such as 2:260 and challenge/showing formulae survive as contrast; they do not recast this imperative as reassurance.

words.gloss_range: accusative masculine dual relative pronoun, the displayed object that controls the later dual chain
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذَيْنِ}} ({{tr:alladhayni}}) gives the request a dual target. Its accusative dual form becomes the hinge for later dual pronouns and verbs, so the ayah tracks the same accused pair from being shown, to being blamed, to being placed, to becoming members of the lowest. The geminated variant and sound rows add apparatus-level weight to that dual boundary, while the canonical accusative dual remains the governing parse.

topics.headline: accusative dual controls the chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the requested object is dual and remains the same pair through the later pronouns and verbs.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the word the explicit second object of the showing imperative, and later dual forms resume it.

topics.headline: two-agent blame target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah concentrates blame into a paired target rather than leaving it as diffuse group accusation.
topics.reason: Semantic and referent rows support paired agency while local grammar keeps the word as a dual relative pronoun.

topics.headline: geminated variant boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant and sound rows thicken the dual boundary as apparatus, while the canonical accusative dual remains the governing parse.
topics.reason: The gemination rows are useful as form contrast but do not control the canonical local morphology.

words.gloss_range: Form IV dual causative misguidance verb with the speakers as affected object
words.root_gloss_range: straying, loss of way, error, and causing to stray; the local Form IV dual selects accused external misguidance rather than simple self-straying
words.prose: {{ar:أَضَلَّانَا}} ({{tr:aḍallānā}}) defines the requested pair by an accusation: they caused us to stray. The Form IV causative and dual subject shift agency onto two blamed misleaders, while the path-loss root keeps the moral error felt as loss of direction. The broader blame scene resembles 7:38, but this wording concentrates the charge into the dual pair and immediately moves toward their source classes.

topics.headline: dual causative blame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the accused pair are defined by causing the speakers to stray.
topics.reason: The Form IV perfect has a dual subject and a first-person plural object, giving the accusation its external misleader grammar.

topics.headline: moral error as lost route
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the misguidance accusation carries path-loss pressure, while local Form IV keeps the sense causative.
topics.reason: The root field supports loss of way and error, but the local form selects causing-to-stray rather than simple wandering.

topics.headline: dualized blame pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a broader judgment-blame pattern, including 7:38, is narrowed here into the two blamed agents.
topics.reason: Concrete blame at 7:38 and local source classification both support the ayah's move from misguidance claim to named source domains.

words.gloss_range: first source/class preposition introducing the jinn-human source phrase for the accused pair
words.prose: The first {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) attaches the accusation to a source/class phrase. It can be heard as from or among, but locally it governs the following jinn-human pair, so the issue is where the accused misleaders come from, not yet what rank they should enter.

topics.headline: source-class preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first source phrase classifies where the accused pair are from.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the preposition governing the jinn noun as a complement to the dual relative phrase.

topics.headline: first half of source-to-rank arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this first from/among phrase will be answered by a second membership phrase at the end.
topics.reason: The repeated-preposition rows connect the first source classification with the final rank classification.

words.gloss_range: definite collective jinn class, governed by the first source preposition and paired with humans
words.root_gloss_range: concealment, hiddenness, jinn, and covered domains; the local definite collective selects the hidden rational class

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: Form IV imperative of showing that makes hidden agency visible

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْجِنِّ}} ({{tr:al-jinni}}) names the hidden side of the source pair. Its definite collective form makes the class recognizable, and its concealment field pushes against {{ar:أَرِنَا}} ({{tr:arinā}}): hidden agency is what the speakers now want exposed. The jinn-human pairing is a known pattern, including the whisperer pairing at 6:112, while 41:29 reverses it into post-verdict blame; the nearby garden promise in 41:30 sharpens the contrast inside the same concealment/garden root field.

topics.headline: hidden collective source class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first accused source domain is a definite hidden collective, not unnamed individuals.
topics.reason: QAC parses a definite singular collective governed by the source preposition, and the root profile supports hiddenness as local pressure.

topics.headline: first half of source binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that hidden jinn come before visible humans, creating a seen-unseen source pair for blame.
topics.reason: The following conjunction coordinates the human class under the same governing phrase, so the word starts a paired source domain.

topics.headline: known jinn-human pairing redirected
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a known jinn-human pairing, including 6:112, is redirected into post-verdict blame and contrasted with 41:30.
topics.reason: Concrete rows cite the whisperer pairing at 6:112 and the contrast with 41:30, while local grammar keeps this word as the first source class.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining the second source class without resetting the governing phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite collective human class coordinated with the jinn source class

words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates {{ar:ٱلْإِنسِ}} ({{tr:al-insi}}) under the same source frame. It adds the human class without restarting the syntax, so the two domains become one paired field of accused misguidance.

topics.headline: second source class joined
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second class is added inside the same source phrase, making one paired accusation field.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the human collective with the jinn collective without resetting the prepositional governance.

words.gloss_range: definite collective human class, coordinated with jinn as the visible-social side of the source pair
words.root_gloss_range: human sociability, familiarity, visibility, and people; the local definite collective selects the human source class while preserving contrast with hiddenness

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: definite collective jinn class paired with the human source class

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِنسِ}} ({{tr:al-insi}}) completes the source binary with the visible, familiar human side. The root pressure around familiarity and sociability survives as contrast with {{ar:ٱلْجِنِّ}} ({{tr:al-jinni}}), while the local grammar keeps the word as a definite collective class, not individual people. The jinn-human formula also recalls 114:6, but here the pair is named by the rejecters as a source of blame.

topics.headline: human collective source class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second source domain is the definite human collective, the visible-social counterpart to the hidden class.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the word a coordinated genitive definite collective under the same source preposition.

topics.headline: familiarity pressure within human class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that familiarity and visible social agency sharpen the human side of the pair, while local grammar still selects the collective class.
topics.reason: The contested human-root pressure survives as contrast with hiddenness; it does not replace the local collective noun function.

topics.headline: jinn-human formula completed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word completes a recurring jinn-human formula, including 114:6, but in 41:29 the formula serves blame.
topics.reason: Concrete rows cite 114:6 and jinn-human polarity, while the local phrase makes the human class the second half of the source merism.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural making/placing verb with a dual object, shifting exposure into intended retaliation
words.root_gloss_range: making, placing, appointing, rendering, and setting; the local frame selects placing/rendering the dual pair underfoot as retaliatory rank assignment
words.prose: {{ar:نَجْعَلْهُمَا}} ({{tr:najʿalhumā}}) turns the request for exposure into a plan for retaliation. The attached dual object resumes the same accused pair, and the making/placing range is locally selected as putting them in a result position underfoot. This human wish to make others low can be heard against divine making scenes such as 95:5 and the same-surah making language at 41:9, but the local agency remains the speakers' desired domination.

topics.headline: same pair made/placed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same dual pair requested for display is now the object of intended placement.
topics.reason: The attached dual object resumes the earlier dual relative, and the following locative phrase supplies the result placement.

topics.headline: making becomes domination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers try to reclaim agency by rendering the accused pair underfoot.
topics.reason: The broad making/placing range is locally selected by the under-feet locative, turning exposure into retaliatory domination.

topics.headline: human wish against divine making
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine making scenes such as 95:5 and 41:9 sharpen the irony, while local agency stays with the speakers' wish.
topics.reason: Rows naming 95:5 and 41:9 survive as contrast and distributional support, not as a replacement for the local first-person plural verb.

words.gloss_range: locative adverb of beneathness, filling the placement result and beginning the spatial demotion image
words.root_gloss_range: below, beneath, under, and lower position; the local locative noun-adverb selects spatial underness with rank-abasement pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: first-person plural making/placing verb with the accused dual as object
definite elative plural class naming the final lowest rank

words.prose: {{ar:تَحْتَ}} ({{tr:taḥta}}) supplies the result location for {{ar:نَجْعَلْهُمَا}} ({{tr:najʿalhumā}}). It is concrete underness before it is rank language: the pair are imagined beneath the speakers' feet, and that physical lower position begins the descent that {{ar:ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ}} ({{tr:al-asfalīn}}) will finish as class status. The usual underness of garden-river blessing or threat settings is inverted here into under-feet humiliation.

topics.headline: under as placement result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that underness is the concrete result location of the making verb.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the under-feet phrase the locative complement of the making verb, with the following feet phrase in construct relation.

topics.headline: physical underness becomes humiliation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that spatial beneathness starts the rank-demotion movement before the final lowest-class word arrives.
topics.reason: The local locative meaning remains concrete, and the surrounding under-feet and lowest-class wording licenses rank-abasement pressure.

topics.headline: under-rivers field inverted
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that familiar underness in blessing or threat settings is inverted here into a wish for under-feet humiliation.
topics.reason: Distributional rows about garden-river and punishment underness survive as contrast, while local syntax selects this specific locative complement.

words.gloss_range: possessed plural feet phrase, making the imagined humiliation bodily and speaker-owned
words.root_gloss_range: foot, step, footing, precedence, and advance; the local plural possessed noun selects bodily feet while allowing precedence reversal pressure
words.prose: {{ar:أَقْدَامِنَا}} ({{tr:aqdāminā}}) makes the demotion bodily and personal. The plural feet match the plural speakers, and the possessive suffix stages the accused pair beneath our feet, not under an abstract rank. The foot/precedence field lets the image imply reversed priority; 10:2 uses footing as true standing with the Lord, while 41:29 turns possessed feet into a wish for domination.

topics.headline: our feet personalize the scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the bodily image belongs to the speakers through the suffix.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after under and carries a first-person plural possessive suffix, tying the placement scene to the speakers.

topics.headline: feet make rank bodily
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the desired abasement is pictured through feet, not an abstract rank term.
topics.reason: The plural possessed feet phrase completes the bodily tableau and conventionally signals domination and humiliation.

topics.headline: footing and precedence reversed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that foot, footing, and precedence pressure make the humiliation a reversal of standing, with 10:2 as a pointed contrast.
topics.reason: The local sense remains bodily feet, while rows naming 10:2 and pleas for firm footing at 2:250 and 3:147 preserve the contrastive footing/standing pressure.

words.gloss_range: purpose/result lām prefixed to the final dual verb, turning placement into a telic sequence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: dual subjunctive being/becoming verb governed by the purpose lām

words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) turns the final clause into purpose or result. It fastens {{ar:يَكُونَا}} ({{tr:yakūnā}}) to the preceding placement, so being among the lowest is not an independent verdict in the quote but the endpoint the speakers want their action to produce.

topics.headline: telic lām governs final state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final lowestness clause is grammatically dependent on the speakers' placement plan.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the lām as governing the following subjunctive dual verb in a purpose clause.

words.gloss_range: dual subjunctive being/becoming verb, carrying the accused pair into a final status predicate
words.root_gloss_range: being, becoming, existing, and state-holding; the local subjunctive dual selects a desired transition into low-status membership

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: purpose/result lām governing the final dual verb
first-person plural making/placing verb that initiates the action-to-state chain
definite elative plural class naming the final lowest rank

words.prose: {{ar:يَكُونَا}} ({{tr:yakūnā}}) carries the dual pair into a status predicate. Governed by {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}), it presents lowestness as the intended outcome; its be/become range makes the under-feet act resolve into a desired state. The local chain from {{ar:نَجْعَلْهُمَا}} ({{tr:najʿalhumā}}) to {{ar:يَكُونَا}} ({{tr:yakūnā}}) to {{ar:ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ}} ({{tr:al-asfalīn}}) turns making into being, with 95:5 providing a pointed contrast for lowest-making.

topics.headline: dual pair enters status predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same accused pair remain dual subjects as they enter the final status clause.
topics.reason: The verb is subjunctive after the purpose lām, with a dual subject and a min-phrase predicate complement.

topics.headline: being becomes status transition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that underfoot placement is meant to become a settled low-status condition.
topics.reason: The be/become range is locally licensed by the purpose clause and the final class predicate.

topics.headline: making seeks being
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the action-to-state sequence from making to being to lowest-class membership, with 95:5 providing a contrastive lowest-making reference.
topics.reason: Rows tie the local chain to making, being, and lowestness; the concrete 95:5 reference sharpens the contrast without controlling the local parse.

words.gloss_range: second preposition marking membership in a rank class rather than source origin

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: dual subjunctive being/becoming verb before the membership phrase
definite elative plural class governed by this second preposition

words.prose: The second {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) no longer marks source. After {{ar:يَكُونَا}} ({{tr:yakūnā}}), it marks membership in {{ar:ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ}} ({{tr:al-asfalīn}}), so the repeated particle frames an arc from where the misleaders are from to what class the speakers want them to enter.

topics.headline: membership preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second preposition classifies the pair among a rank group rather than locating them physically.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the preposition govern the final adjective plural as predicate complement of the being verb.

topics.headline: second half of min arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated preposition shifting from source origin to endpoint rank.
topics.reason: The local repetition makes the first phrase name where the accused are from and the second phrase name the class they should enter.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine sound plural elative class, naming the lowest as the final rank category
words.root_gloss_range: lowness, bottomness, baseness, and lower rank; the local elative plural selects extreme low-rank class membership
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ}} ({{tr:al-asfalīn}}) is the quoted speech's final landing point. Its definite elative plural names an identifiable class of the lowest, not a vague low place, and it turns the bodily under-feet image into moral rank. The rare low-rank field, the making-to-being chain, and the echo of 95:5 sharpen the reversal: in 41:29 the rejecters want to administer lowestness to others, and the ayah closes on that exposed hierarchy.

topics.headline: definite plural lowest class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the endpoint is membership in an identifiable class of the lowest, not a vague low condition.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence parse the word as a definite masculine sound plural elative governed by the second preposition as predicate class.

topics.headline: underness resolves as moral rank
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that physical descent under the feet becomes categorical abasement at the ayah boundary.
topics.reason: The s-f-l field supports low place and baseness, and the local sequence from underness to lowest class licenses both without flattening the elative force.

topics.headline: rare elative closes the quote
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final rare low-rank word gives the quote a marked descent, with 95:5 reframed as the rejecters' wish for others.
topics.reason: Rows naming 95:5, rare distribution, and final sound closure support the closing payoff while local grammar keeps the word as the final class predicate.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: أَضَلَّانَا ... نَجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ أَقْدَامِنَا ... مِنَ ٱلْأَسْفَلِينَ
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers convert attributed causal precedence into punitive spatial and social inferiority: the pair credited with directing them away is to be remade as a trampled lower rank.

activation_trace.role: Deviation from guidance supplies the directional harm attributed to the pair.
Making something assume a condition supplies the deliberate conversion of the pair's rank.
The physically lower direction supplies the geometry of subordination.
The foot that treads supplies the bodily interface of punitive domination.
Lowness of social standing converts the bodily image into degradation of status.

changed_reading.before: They ask that two misleaders be punished.
changed_reading.after: They script punishment as a vertical reversal in which blamed guides are converted into a trampled lower class so the speakers recover relative precedence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ... أَرِنَا ... مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ
baseline_models.mechanism: Truth-coverers ask for an act of showing that exposes agency across the hidden jinn and manifest human poles; the request reverses concealment before it proceeds to punishment.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the speakers' own relation to what has been obscured.
Causing something to be seen supplies the requested reversal from concealment to exposure.
Hiddenness from sense supplies the concealed pole of the blamed agency.
Manifest humanity opposed to the jinn supplies the perceptible pole of the pair.

changed_reading.before: The speakers merely request identification of two culprits from jinn and humankind.
changed_reading.after: Their request is a counter-concealment operation: people defined by covering ask that hidden and manifest channels of agency be made perceptible.

baseline_models.mechanism: The switch from an imperative addressed to the sovereign Lord to first-person plural making divides the act: divine authority is asked to disclose the targets, while the petitioners reserve their demotion for themselves.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies the public petition that assigns roles.
Lordship and sovereignty supply the authority from whom disclosure is requested.
Showing supplies the divine epistemic act requested by the speakers.
Assigning a condition supplies the retaliatory act the speakers claim for themselves.

changed_reading.before: They ask God to punish their misleaders.
changed_reading.after: They ask God for evidentiary access, then imagine themselves executing the status reversal; the prayer preserves rather than surrenders their will to dominate.

context_deltas.mechanism: The demand for showing follows both a declared sensory enclosure and an organized attempt to manufacture it: covered hearts, weighted ears, a barrier, prohibited listening, and noise aimed at prevailing. Their lack of sight is therefore partly an achieved policy, not merely something done to them.

activation_trace.role: Requested showing supplies the belated demand for perceptual access.
A protective cover supplies the speakers' announced enclosure of their hearts.
Weight in the ear supplies their claimed auditory blockage.
A screening barrier supplies the declared separation from the message.
Hearing as understanding and response supplies the reception they order others to withhold.
Mixed clamor supplies the active production of auditory occlusion.
Conquering force supplies the strategic aim of the manufactured blockage.

structural_cues: 41:5's enclosure claims and 41:26's no-listening command precede 41:29's imperative أَرِنَا.
The sensory sequence moves from refusing reception to demanding visual disclosure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covers, ear-weight, barrier, prohibited listening, clamor, and the later request to be shown; I infer that the epistemic deficit is partly self-produced. A live alternative is that these are collective portraits rather than the conduct of every individual speaker.

changed_reading.before: They need revelation because the agents who misled them are hidden.
changed_reading.after: Their demand for sight also indicts a prior policy of blocking reception: they ask for disclosure only after declaring and weaponizing occlusion.

context_deltas.mechanism: Just before the focus, sensory faculties and skins become speaking witnesses to what their owners did. The foot in the focus can no longer function as an innocent instrument for exporting blame: embodied agency has already become evidence against the agent.

activation_trace.role: The treading foot supplies the bodily instrument the speakers recruit for retaliation.
Presence with witnessed perception turns the body scene into an evidentiary mechanism.
The body's skin supplies an intimate witness that cannot be displaced onto an external culprit.
Intentional deed supplies what the embodied witnesses disclose.
Speech made possible for the skins supplies the body's conversion from instrument to witness.

structural_cues: 41:20-22 foreground hearing, sight, and skin immediately before 41:29 foregrounds feet.
The testimony is explicitly tied to what the speakers themselves had been doing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies bodily testimony to deeds and a later treading foot; I extend the evidentiary force from the named faculties and skin to embodied action generally. The live alternative is that the passage never says the feet themselves testify.

changed_reading.before: Their feet are neutral instruments for punishing the guilty pair.
changed_reading.after: The underfoot fantasy uses a body already implicated as counterwitness, so the gesture cannot cleanly transfer culpability away from the speakers' own action.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah repeatedly assigns an inward share of causality: blindness is preferred, outcomes are earned, a supposition about the Lord causes ruin, and evil returns upon the self. The two misleaders remain possible causes, but the focus cry concentrates a distributed causal field onto two punishable bodies.

activation_trace.role: Departure from guidance supplies the harm the speakers attribute externally.
Love lodged in the heart supplies active preference rather than passive victimhood.
Blindness of insight supplies the state that is chosen over guidance.
Acquisition by one's effort supplies responsibility for the resulting state.
Unsecured supposition supplies an internal cognitive cause.
Falling into destruction supplies the explicit effect of that supposition.
The self as the very person supplies the destination of moral consequence.
The act that causes harm supplies what returns against its doer.

structural_cues: The focus uses a causative verb with two external subjects, while 41:23 gives the speakers' own supposition an explicit destructive predicate.
41:17 and 41:46 frame blindness and harm through preference, earning, and return to self.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies several explicit inward causal links; I infer that 41:29 selectively compresses them into an accusation against two agents. The live alternative is additive causality: external seduction and accountable assent can both be fully operative.

changed_reading.before: Two external agents caused the fall and therefore deserve concentrated retaliation.
changed_reading.after: The accusation is a blame-concentration move inside distributed causality: companions may mislead, but preference, earning, supposition, and self-returning action prevent the speakers from becoming mere victims.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding companions are attached alongside the people and beautify the field before and behind them. The focus then remaps that intimate lateral and temporal enclosure into a vertical one: those who occupied the horizon are to be moved underfoot.

activation_trace.role: A companion joined to a companion supplies proximate attachment rather than remote command.
Making something appear beautiful supplies the perceptual mechanism of misdirection.
What lies before the hands supplies the forward part of the framed horizon.
What lies behind supplies the rear or past-facing part of the same enclosure.
The hidden jinn class supplies one repeated domain from which the focus names its blamed pair.
Manifest humankind supplies the other repeated domain of the focus accusation.
The lower direction supplies the destination imposed on formerly adjacent companions.
Precedence and rank within the foot branch sharpen the reversal from influential proximity to inferior status.

structural_cues: 41:25 immediately precedes the punishment sequence and repeats ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلْإِنسِ before 41:29.
The spatial-temporal pair before/behind is answered by the focus's under/feet.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies attached companions, beautification, front and rear, then underfoot; I infer a topological reversal from surrounding proximity to vertical subordination. Front and rear may primarily denote future and past, but that alternative still supports control of the speakers' temporal horizon.

changed_reading.before: The misleaders are superior commanders who directed followers from above.
changed_reading.after: They appear as attached companions whose beautification occupied the speakers' front-and-back horizon; the punishment fantasy converts intimacy and framing into inferiority.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same class formula introduces unbelievers who command others not to listen, to drown the recitation in noise, and thereby prevail. In the focus they speak as the misled; packet sequence makes the accusation recursive because the accusers have occupied the social role of misleaders.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies the accusation voiced by the unbelieving collective.
Deviation from guidance supplies the role they assign exclusively to the blamed pair.
The repeated speech act supplies the collective's own directive intervention.
Obstruction of truth supplies the shared subject class across directive and accusation.
Hearing as comprehension supplies the reception they try to prevent in others.
Deflection from the right course supplies their active method of misleading.
Prevailing by force supplies the intended social effect of that deflection.

structural_cues: 41:26 and 41:29 both begin with the same وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ formula.
The first speech directs others away from reception; the second identifies others as those who directed the speakers away.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated class formula and the two speech acts; I infer role recursion at the collective level. This does not prove that each individual in the eschatological crowd personally issued the earlier command.

changed_reading.before: The speakers are victims seeking the agents who misled them.
changed_reading.after: They are accusers from a collective already shown manufacturing misguidance, so their complaint is also a perpetrator's attempt to isolate blame in someone else.

context_deltas.mechanism: Adjacent speeches share the saying of 'our Lord' but diverge in motion. In the focus, the address launches a plan to put others below; in 41:30, saying 'our Lord is God' continues into rectitude and a consoling descent of angels. The truth of the address is disclosed by its trajectory.

activation_trace.role: Uttered speech supplies the first 'our Lord' formula.
Lordship supplies the shared address whose consequences diverge.
Social baseness supplies the downward outcome sought by the first speech.
Degraded standing completes the first speech's trajectory.
The repeated utterance supplies the contrasting 'our Lord is God' formula.
The same lordship branch makes the contrast depend on what follows the address, not on the noun alone.
Straightness and balance supply the embodied sequel to the faithful confession.
Beneficent descent supplies a downward movement opposite in function to forced degradation.

structural_cues: 41:29 and 41:30 are adjacent and repeat قالوا ربنا.
The first continuation is underfoot and lowest; the second is rectitude followed by angelic descent.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the adjacent formula and opposed motions; I read the juxtaposition as testing confession by its sequel. A live alternative is that 41:30 simply contrasts a different group without directly glossing the prior address.

changed_reading.before: Calling on 'our Lord' marks a repentant or faithful turn by the punished speakers.
changed_reading.after: The address alone proves little: here it serves retaliatory hierarchy, whereas the next 'our Lord' becomes credible through rectitude and a descent that consoles rather than degrades.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later vertical instruction directs people to lower themselves before the Creator, while arrogance is the refusal. The focus instead seeks elevation through the forced lowering of others, exposing two opposed uses of verticality: worshipful self-abasement and retaliatory status domination.

activation_trace.role: The lower direction supplies the position imposed on someone else.
The treading foot supplies the speakers' retained bodily elevation.
Degraded standing supplies the outcome assigned to the other.
Voluntary lowering supplies the commanded bodily relation when directed to God rather than created powers.
Submissive worship supplies the purpose of self-lowering.
Pride and self-magnification supply the resistance to that posture.

structural_cues: The focus's feet remain above while others are forced below; 41:37 commands the addressee's own prostration.
41:38 immediately names arrogant refusal before contrasting worship near the Lord.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies forced other-lowering, commanded self-lowering, and arrogance; I infer a vertical ethic contrasting domination with worship. The later command addresses a living audience, so it is a thematic countermodel rather than a claim that the damned could perform it then.

changed_reading.before: Putting the misleaders underfoot is simply proportionate humiliation.
changed_reading.after: The wish preserves an arrogant vertical logic: the speakers seek height by lowering others, whereas the surah's proper bodily descent is one's own submission to the Creator.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus proposes transforming a hostile relation by changing the enemy's rank; 41:34 proposes transforming it by a better response until hostility becomes intimate alliance. These are competing causal mechanisms for what to do with an adversarial other.

activation_trace.role: Making another assume a status supplies coercive relational transformation.
Degraded social rank supplies the only endpoint imagined for the hostile pair.
Doing the good supplies the alternative input that changes the relation.
Pushing away harm supplies a response that resists without placing the other beneath oneself.
Enmity supplies the initial relation shared by the countermodel.
Affection and support supply the transformed relation.
Intimate closeness supplies the endpoint opposite to degraded distance.

structural_cues: Both passages contain a relational conversion: make the blamed pair lowest versus make an enemy like an intimate ally.
The two mechanisms preserve multiplicity rather than yielding a single rule for eschatological and present conflict.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two explicit transformations of an adversarial relation; I set them in contrast. A materially live alternative is that 41:29 describes irreversible eschatological accusation while 41:34 governs present ethical response, limiting direct transfer.

changed_reading.before: Their proposed humiliation straightforwardly models just relational reversal.
changed_reading.after: It also reads as speech still unable to imagine relation except through rank domination, sharply unlike the later mechanism that converts enmity through a better response.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus asks for external persons to be shown as the explanation of error. The surah's close reuses seeing and astrayness but redirects disclosure: the deeply astray subject is in distant rupture, and God shows signs in horizons and selves until truth becomes clear. Seeing culprits is displaced by seeing evidence and oneself.

activation_trace.role: Causing another to see supplies the focus request for external disclosure.
Departure from guidance supplies the condition they explain through two others.
Interrogative attention supplies a demand that the addressees examine their own premise.
Straying now characterizes the opposed subject rather than only an effect imposed by a named pair.
A group split by opposition supplies the subject's own relational location in error.
Distance from nearness supplies the depth of that self-location.
Divine showing supplies the answer to the focus's demand but changes what is shown.
The person's own self supplies an inward field of evidence.
Emergence into clarity supplies the result of that redirected showing.
Stable truth matching reality supplies the object ultimately disclosed.

structural_cues: أَرِنَا in 41:29 and سَنُرِيهِمْ in 41:53 share the causative seeing construction.
أَضَلَّانَا in 41:29 and أَضَلُّ in 41:52 share the straying root while changing causal syntax.
The requested object shifts from two others to signs in horizons and selves.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the root echoes and changed objects of showing; I infer an epistemic correction from scapegoat-visibility to truth- and self-visibility. The external signs do not cancel the reality of external tempters, so this is redirection rather than disproof.

changed_reading.before: Truth will arrive once the speakers can see the two people responsible for their error.
changed_reading.after: The surah answers that demand by changing the field of vision: decisive showing concerns signs, the self, and truth, while deepest straying is located in the subject's own distant rupture.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The valency reversal is surprising: the focus has agents causing people to stray, whereas 41:48 has invoked objects themselves go missing from their callers. It remains anchored by the exact ض ل ل root and the focus's demand to locate blamed agents, but downstream prose must treat it as a root-level echo and must not identify what was invoked in 41:48 with the exact pair in 41:29.

activation_trace.role: Showing supplies the attempt to locate and expose the blamed pair.
Deviation from guidance supplies the causative accusation.
Loss of a thing from its owner reverses the root so the relied-on objects become unlocatable.
Calling by speech supplies the failed relation to what disappears.
Turning aside from a direction supplies the absence of an escape route after the disappearance.

changed_reading.before: The speakers can restore order by locating the agents who made them lose the way.
changed_reading.after: The root echo permits a more unstable picture: callers, called objects, and guides inhabit reciprocal lostness, so locating two culprits cannot by itself recover an exit.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates the packet's non-dominant mapping of focus ر ب ب to ر ب و through 41:39's rising earth; it is not a claim that رَبَّنَا lexically means the earth rose. It remains valid as a packet-authorized cross-root image anchored in رَبَّنَا and the focus's downward lexicon, and downstream prose should label it explicitly as an exploratory vertical resonance.

activation_trace.role: Increase and elevation supply a latent upward branch inside the packet's split mapping for the divine address.
Being made to descend supplies the punitive downward vector opposed to that branch.
The earth's life-bearing motion supplies the transition from low stillness to animation.
Increase and rising in the earth make the non-dominant focus branch contextually active.

changed_reading.before: The invocation of the Lord simply authorizes a request to force others downward.
changed_reading.after: An exploratory branch hears an inversion: the address carries a latent image of generative rising, activated by earth swelling to life, while the speakers can imagine vertical power only as making others descend.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The cross-scene pattern is surprising because it links cosmological association in 41:9 with eschatological retaliation in 41:29 through repeated ج ع ل. It remains anchored in the exact making verb and rank language, but the second-person audience and later collective need not be identical individuals; render it as a discourse-level compulsion to manipulate rank, not as a biographical claim.

activation_trace.role: Assigning a condition or rank supplies the intended demotion of the blamed pair.
Low social standing supplies the endpoint of the later rank assignment.
The same status-making branch supplies the earlier assignment of peers to the Lord.
A rival counterpart supplies the falsely elevated rank created in the earlier scene.
Sovereign lordship supplies the rank against which peers are improperly made.

changed_reading.before: The underfoot request is an isolated wish for retribution.
changed_reading.after: It can also be heard as the late form of a rank-making compulsion: first assigning rivals beside the Lord, then assigning blamed guides beneath the self.

strongest_changes: The request to be shown follows self-declared covers and a deliberate no-listening noise strategy, making ignorance partly manufactured.
41:17, 41:23, and 41:46 redistribute causality back through preference, earning, supposition, and consequence to self.
41:25 changes remote leaders into attached companions who beautify the front-and-back horizon before being topologically reassigned underfoot.
Bodily testimony makes the retaliatory foot part of implicated embodied agency rather than a neutral instrument.
The closing reuse of causative seeing redirects disclosure from two external culprits toward signs, the self, and truth.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet activated a coherent set of causal and spatial reversals: concealment to showing, companionate surround to underfoot rank, self-lowering to other-lowering, and external accusation to inward disclosure. It also preserved two useful oddities: reciprocal lostness under ض ل ل and the packet-authorized ر ب ب/ر ب و rising branch.
remaining_uncertainties: The dual may denote a representative jinn-human pair, but 41:25's plural communities do not identify the exact two.
The repeated unbelieving collective in 41:26 and 41:29 supports role recursion without proving identical individual speakers.
Underfoot may function chiefly as an idiom of humiliation, which limits the body-witness extension from skin and faculties to feet.
The ر ب ب to ر ب و elevation model is intentionally exploratory and must not be rendered as direct lexical equivalence.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The hidden causes of error are demanded as visible objects.** **ض ل ل B001** gives going astray and **ض ل ل B002** hiding or disappearing; **ج ن ن B005** hidden beings and **ء ن س B001** visible human presence; **ر ء ي B012** showing and making seen. The request seeks both hidden and visible misleaders in one field of sight. I infer that judgment removes the invisibility by which agency was displaced. The ayah reads as forced causal disclosure.
2. **Blame seeks a spatial status reversal.** **ت ح ت B001/B002** gives under-position and lowly people; **ق د م B001/B002** foot and precedent standing; **س ف ل B001/B002** low place and low rank. They want former guides beneath their feet. I infer that their proposed justice is a vertical inversion of dependence, converting followers into superiors. The request reveals continued status-thinking rather than recovered responsibility.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:34 later offers a non-coercive transformation of enmity into nearness, exposing how different the punitive reversal here is from genuine relational repair. 41:48 then says the invoked objects simply disappear, denying even this fantasy of restored superiority.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Moral blame is externalized as a vertical hierarchy.** Lexically, `ض ل ل B001` is leading away from guidance and aim, `ق د م B001` the foot used for treading, `ت ح ت B001` what is under the feet, and `س ف ل B002` low rank and baseness. Structurally, the companions of 41:25 are now requested as visible objects beneath the speakers’ feet; 41:30 answers with people who remain upright and receive supportive accompaniment. I assign the feet the role of imposed dominance and lowness the role of converting causal blame into status. The inferred arrow is that placing misleaders below attempts to transfer responsibility while preserving the speakers’ superiority. The ayah reads as a last hierarchical reordering of a shared error, not repentance from it.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 41:30’s upright stance reversed the wish to put others underfoot, and 41:34’s conversion of an enemy into an ally corrected the remaining hierarchy: the alternative to misguidance is not better domination but transformed relation.

baseline.text: İnkâr edenler, Rabbimiz! Bizi saptıran cin ve insanlardan olan o ikisini bize göster; en aşağıdakilerden olsunlar diye onları ayaklarımızın altına alalım, derler.

findings.text: Yargı anındaki istek, sapmanın gizli ve görünür aracılarının aynı görüş alanında açığa çıkarılmasını talep ederek sorumluluğun saklı nedenlerini görünür kılar.
Saptıranları ayak altına alma isteği, ortak sorumluluğu kabul etmek yerine eski önderleri aşağı indirerek üstünlüğü geri kazanmayı amaçlayan bir konum değişimidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal çıplak söz söyleme ve söylenmiş söz çekirdeğidir; organ, unvan, söylenti ve mecazlar ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım çıplak söyleme ve sözlü ifade anlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşünceyi veya sözü sesli biçimde dışa vurma ve böyle dışa vurulmuş harfli sözlü ifade anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
Söylenen şey tek söz, cümle, şiir veya konuşma ölçeğinde olabilir.
Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sözü sesle dışa çıkarılan ve harflerden oluşan sözlü ifade çekirdeğinde toplar; ad biçimleri de aynı alana bağlıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Fiilsel söyleme işlemini korur.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.

Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da gözle görülen düzensiz bir sarsılma veya titreme görünümü taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda nesne ve fiziksel kararsızlık kurucudur; komşu kolda insan bedeni ile korku veya öfke nedeni kurucudur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi örtme ve görünmez kılma çekirdeğini; zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme, külün toprakla kapanması ve yıldızların güneş ışığında görünmemesi gibi gerçekleşmelerle açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek fiziksel örtmedir; dinî inkâr, nimeti yadsıma ve günahı giderme bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın örtme çekirdeğini korur; zırh, silah, kül ve gök cisimleriyle ilgili kullanımlar bu çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleri olarak ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeyle örterek görünmesini engellemek veya kapalı duruma getirmektir. Zırhın giysiyle, kişinin silahla ya da külün savrulan toprakla örtülmesi bu işlemin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin üstünü kapatarak onu görünmez veya örtülü duruma getirme işlemi.
Zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme ve külün üstünün toprakla kapanması çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
Güneşin yıldızları görünmez kılması da görsel örtme sonucu üzerinden bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar örtme ve kapatma çekirdeğinde birleşir; farklı örnekler bu işlemin nesne, giysi, silah, kül ve gök görünümü üzerindeki gerçekleşmelerini gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin üstünü başka bir şeyle kapatıp görünmesini engelleyen genel çekirdek için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Örtme işlemini ve görünürlüğün engellenmesi sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Zırhın giysiyle veya külün toprakla kaplanması gibi somut bağlamlarda doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Somut bir nesnenin üstünün kapatılması işlemini eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Güneş ışığının yıldızları görünmez kıldığı göksel bağlamda sonuç odaklı doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Görsel örtmenin görünürlüğü ortadan kaldıran sonucunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal zırh, silah, kül ve güneş ışığı gibi belirli gerçekleşmeleri de taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal haber veya tanıklığı gizleme ve örtü adı gibi daha geniş kullanımlara da uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalın çekirdeğinde bir şeyi örterek görünmesini engelleme vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Çekirdek büyük ölçüde örtüşür; ancak komşu dal soyut gizlemeyi ve örtü nesnelerini de kapsarken bu dalın kanıtı belirli somut ve görsel gerçekleşmelere dayanır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi karanlık geceyi, denizi, büyük ırmağı, gün batımını ve bulutu aynı adlandırma çevresinde toplar; bunların tümünü tek bir gerçek 'kuşatan örtü' türü saymak yerine, karanlık, genişlik veya kapatma etkisiyle örten farklı varlıklar olarak anlamak gerekir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel karanlık ya da genel su kütlesi değildir; kaynakta örtücü etkisiyle adlandırılan belirli varlıklarla sınırlıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal, kaynakta doğrudan adlandırılan gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı ve bulut kapsamıyla tanımlanır; yapıya özgü başka anlam eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Karanlığı, genişliği veya kapatma etkisi nedeniyle kişileri ya da görünümü örten karanlık gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı veya bulut için kullanılan bir nitelemedir.

facets.statement: Karanlık, genişlik ya da kapatma etkisiyle başka şeylerin görünmesini veya seçilmesini engelleyen varlık.
Gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı ve bulut kaynaklarda bu nitelemenin farklı gönderimleri olarak sıralanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar aynı sözü karanlık gece, deniz ve büyük ırmak için verir; bazı aktarımlar gün batımını ve bulutu da örtücü etkileri nedeniyle bu listeye ekler.

concept_gloss.applicability: Farklı gönderimleri tek bir nesne türüne indirgemeden ortak örtücü etkiyi anlatmak için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Karanlık ve genişlik yoluyla örtme ortaklığını, gönderim çeşitliliğiyle birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sözün karanlık geceyi nitelediği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gecenin karanlığıyla kişileri ve görünümü örtmesi özelliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı ve bulut gönderimlerini dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sözün deniz veya büyük ırmak için kullanıldığı bağlamlarda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Deniz ve büyük ırmak gönderimlerinin genişlik ve kuşatıcılık yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Gece, gün batımı ve bulut gönderimlerini dışarıda bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı inancın karşıtı ve gerçeğin örtülmesi olarak tanımlar; birliği, dinî hükmü veya peygamberliği yadsıma ile inkâr, bile bile direnme, ikiyüzlülük ve ortak koşma türlerini açıkça içerir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal dinî gerçeği ve inancı reddetmeyle sınırlıdır; nimeti yadsıma veya yalnızca genel bir gerçeği inkâr etme bunun tamamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dinî reddetme çekirdeği korunur; kalben bilip söylememe, bilip kabul etmeme, dıştan inanmış görünme ve hem kalple hem dille reddetme yapıya bağlı türlerdir.

concept_map.definition: İnancı, birliği, dinî hükmü veya peygamberliği reddederek dinî gerçeği örtmek ya da kabul etmemektir. Kaynaklar bunu inkâr, bile bile direnme, ikiyüzlülük, ortak koşma ve yalanlama gibi türlere ayırır.

facets.statement: İnancın karşıtı olarak dinî gerçeği, birliği, dinî hükmü veya peygamberliği reddetme.
Kalben bilip sözle kabul etmeme, bilip boyun eğmeme, dıştan inanmış görünme ve hem kalple hem dille inkâr etme farklı türlerdir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar dalı inancın karşıtı sayar ve gerçeği örtme düşüncesiyle açıklar; toplu aktarım çeşitli inkâr, direnme ve ikiyüzlülük biçimlerini de sıralar.

concept_gloss.applicability: İnancın karşıtı olan çekirdeği ve reddedilen dinî içeriği birlikte ifade eder.

error_profile.preserves: Dinî gerçeği kabul etmeme çekirdeğini ve inanç karşıtlığını korur.

error_profile.loses: İkiyüzlülük ve bütünüyle bilgisiz inkâr gibi öteki türleri dışarıda bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi nimeti yadsımayı, onu örtmeyi ve gereği olan şükrü yerine getirmemeyi aynı çekirdekte birleştirir; dalın geçici çerçevesi bu koşulu doğru yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Nesne özellikle nimettir ve belirleyici sonuç şükrün terkidir; genel dinî ret bu dala kendiliğinden girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Nimeti yadsıma çekirdeği yalın ve türemiş kullanımlarda korunur; nimetle kurulan yapı ve aşırılık bildiren kişi nitelemesi ayrı gerçekleşmelerdir.

concept_map.definition: Bir nimeti tanımamak, değerini örtmek veya onun gerektirdiği şükrü yerine getirmemektir. Bu tutumda aşırı olan kişi de aynı anlam alanında nitelenir.

facets.statement: Bir nimeti yadsıma veya şükrünü yerine getirmeyerek değerini örtme.

concept_gloss.applicability: Nimeti tanımama ile ona şükretmeme çekirdeğini kısa ve doğal biçimde verir.

error_profile.preserves: Nimetin inkâr edilmesini ve şükrün terk edilmesini birlikte korur.
